items.stem: Which of the following is a physical change according to the passage?
Based on the passage, what can be concluded about the mass of water formed when hydrogen and oxygen combine?
Which of the following best describes a chemical change according to the passage?

According to the passage, what is the main reason atoms combine to form compounds?
If 2 g of hydrogen combines with 16 g of oxygen to form 18 g of water, what does this illustrate about the combination of atoms?
What is the significance of the Law of Definite Proportions mentioned in the passage?
What does the passage say about the formation of a hydrogen molecule?
Which of the following is a correct way to name a covalent compound?
What is the charge on a chloride anion formed by a chlorine atom?
Which of the following best describes the type of bond in a solid compound that does not conduct electricity in the solid state but conducts when dissolved in water?
What is the main idea of the passage about the Law of Conservation of Mass?
According to the passage, what is the formula unit mass of potassium chloride (KCl)?

Which of the following is an example of a covalent compound?
If element A has one electron in its third shell and element B has six electrons in its second shell, which of the following combinations would form a stable ionic compound?
Which of the following statements is true about ionic compounds?
Based on the passage, what can be inferred about the solubility of ionic compounds?
If a compound is found to conduct electricity when dissolved in water but not in the solid state, what type of compound is it most likely to be?
How many hydroxide ions (OH⁻) are needed to combine with one magnesium ion (Mg²⁺) to form a neutral compound?
What is the name of the law that states that matter can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction?
A compound consists of 40% sulfur and 60% oxygen by mass. In a sample containing 20 g of sulfur, how much oxygen is needed to satisfy the Law of Constant Proportions?
In a chemical reaction, a student burns 10 g of ethanol in an open beaker, and no residue is left. Does this mean the Law of Conservation of Mass is violated?
What is the name of the ion formed when a chlorine atom accepts one electron?
What type of bond is formed between hydrogen and chlorine atoms in a hydrogen chloride molecule?
Which ion is formed when a chlorine atom accepts one electron?
What is the correct name of the compound formed between magnesium and chlorine?
According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, what is the relationship between the mass of reactants and the mass of products in a chemical reaction?
What happens to the mass of the system during a chemical reaction when the gas produced is not allowed to escape?
Which of the following compounds is formed when magnesium gives two electrons and chlorine takes one electron?
If a student conducts an experiment with vinegar and baking soda but does not seal the container, what will happen to the mass measured after the reaction?
